faq: Either the surface (arc) distance or the central angle — they convert into each other through the radius, and the chord follows from 2R sin(θ/2).
Why is the chord never longer than the arc?
A straight line is the shortest path between two points in space; the arc is constrained to the sphere's surface. The chord wins every time the angle is nonzero.
The mean radius 6,371.01 km, matching this family's other Earth-geometry pages so their numbers cross-check exactly.
How deep does the NYC–LA tunnel go?
307.4 km at midpoint — the sagitta of that chord. Depth grows fast: a 90° chord bottoms out about 1,866 km down, in the lower mantle.
Do any real tunnels use this?
None through the planet — but neutrino detectors and seismic stations live on chord geometry, and the chord is the reference every 'straight through' claim is measured against.
Exactly the diameter: 12,742.02 km on the mean sphere. Every antipode pair shares it.
The real Earth's polar and equatorial diameters differ by about 43 km; chord work at the precision where that matters is geodesy, and this page's spherical framing is stated on it.
